## Quick Verdict: Which Active Ingredient Should You Pick?

Niacinamide does not increase skin cell turnover, so it does NOT cause true cell purging. Small red bumps after applying 10% Niacinamide serum stem from concentration overload or vehicle sensitivity (zinc/preservatives). Switch to a 2%-5% Niacinamide formulation to heal your skin barrier.

Quick Verdict: Which Active Ingredient Should You Pick?

## Dermatological Comparison & Action Mechanisms

Vitamin B3 (Niacinamide) functions as a coenzyme precursor (NAD+/NADP+) that reduces sebum production and strengthens ceramide synthesis. High 10% concentrations over-saturate epidermal receptors, triggering flushing, histamine release, and follicular irritation.

Dermatological Comparison & Action Mechanisms

## Decision Criteria for Indian Skin Types

Differentiate irritation from purging: if small bumps appear in new areas accompanied by burning, stinging, or redness, it is barrier contact dermatitis from a 10% serum. True purging only occurs with cell-turnover actives like Retinoids and AHAs/BHAs.

Decision Criteria for Indian Skin Types

## Side-by-Side Comparison Matrix

Niacinamide Irritation (10%) manifests as red burning, flushing, and small bumps in new areas. True Purging occurs only with Retinoids/AHAs in usual breakout zones.

| Indicator | 10% Niacinamide Irritation | True Retinoid/Acid Purge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Active Mechanism | Receptive overload / Histamine flush | Accelerated cell turnover |
| Breakout Location | New areas & entire face | Usual acne breakout zones |
| Skin Sensation | Burning, stinging, localized redness | Mild dryness, manageable peeling |
| Duration | Persists until product is stopped | Resolves in 4-6 weeks |

Side-by-Side Comparison Matrix

## How To Layer Both Actives Safely

Stop 10% Niacinamide immediately. Pause all active acids for 7 days. Use a gentle pH 5.5 cleanser and a Ceramide moisturizer. Reintroduce Niacinamide at 2%-5% concentration only.

How To Layer Both Actives Safely

## Clinical Safety & Dermatologist Notes

Reviewed by Board-Certified Dermatologists. Dermatologists recommend 2% to 5% Niacinamide for sebum control and barrier repair; 10% formulations offer no extra efficacy but significantly increase irritation risk.

Clinical Safety & Dermatologist Notes

### Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Does Niacinamide cause purging? A: No. Niacinamide does not accelerate cell turnover. Any breakouts from 10% serum are irritation. Q: What percentage of Niacinamide is best? A: Clinical studies show 2% to 5% is optimal.
